**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The IP architecture in this agreement already sits at the playbook's preferred position, and every material term runs in our favour:

- **Deliverables assigned to us** — §13.1 (p0197): MSL assigns all intellectual and industrial property rights in hardware, software, design and documentation of all Products delivered.
- **Inventions captured** — p0198: IBM owns (and MSL assigns) inventions made on Products and on IBM processes/systems, with MSL retaining only a use right for performing the work; MSL is also barred from using proprietary assembly/test processes.
- **Our pre-existing IP ring-fenced** — §13.3(a) (p0208): no rights or licences in IBM pre-existing IP except a royalty-free licence to use disclosed confidential information under the AECI solely to manufacture Products for IBM; anything further needs a separate signed agreement.
- **Tooling and loaned items** — SOW §21.1(e) (p1105): tooling purchased, furnished, charged to or paid for by IBM becomes and remains IBM property. Loan Agreement §5 (p1530): IBM retains title to all Loaned Items, no MSL transfer rights. MSL's ownership of generic "Common Tooling" (p1088) is the vendor-tools carve-out the playbook expressly accepts.
- **No walk-away triggers**: no assignment of IBM IP or data to MSL anywhere in the document, and no joint ownership.

Two minor sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with the playbook's treatment of sub-preferred details: there is no express licence-back of MSL background IP embedded in Products (largely mitigated by the breadth of the §13.1 assignment and the proprietary-process bar), and there is no standalone Customer Data ownership sentence — expected in a 1998 manufacturing outsourcing deal where information flows are governed by the AECI with return-on-demand rights.
